Guidance.Heading: Source and citation convention
Guidance.Text:
- Source: `eASLRB_v3_01.pdf`, delivery edition 3.01, 716 physical PDF pages. The credits themselves read Version 3.0, June 2025.
- Verified SHA-256: `957de75be52c34a7de4c20e875d33145e6b7d4ff8f19384c68818e385d41a247`.
- Initial scan and review: 2026-10-25; expanded-term audit and remaining-510 passage review: 2026-10-26. The scan covers the complete PDF text, not just the repository conversion of Chapters A to E.
- `p.` and `pp.` mean physical PDF pages, counted from 1. Printed page labels, such as H11 or W13, differ.
- A reference such as `A10.2` identifies the chapter and rule. A range such as `C8.1-.2` preserves the source shorthand for C8.1 through C8.2. Page locators attached to numbered references identify verified rule headings; a rule may continue onto the next page. National vehicle/ordnance notes and named chart keys are cited by name and physical page because they are also sources of definitions.
- The Index and Glossary on pp. 11-42 supplies both definitions and a map of application rules. The numbered references retained below include its secondary applications and exceptions. These are supporting reference trails, not a claim that every cited rule independently spells out the acronym.
- References to Chapters O, P, Q, R, S, T, their CG rules, and module SSRs are reproduced as index locators. This PDF lists those chapters in its contents and index but does not include their rule text. The glossary can establish an expansion; those external module rules cannot be independently verified from this PDF.
- A missing rule number in the index is a search lead. Both the abbreviation and its expanded name must be checked in the rule text, notes, training material, and charts. Where the definition is in an unnumbered introduction or key, the reference names that passage and its physical page.
- Some familiar historical or publication abbreviations are used without being expanded in the PDF. Where a conventional expansion is supplied, the entry identifies it as such and cites the original usage separately. Equipment codes that lack a spelled-out expansion are explained from their equipment notes rather than assigned an invented expansion.
- Ordinary capitalized rule terms, Roman-numeral model numbers, hex coordinates, counter ID letters, chart case letters, personal initials, and printing artifacts are not acronyms. Compound vehicle Type codes combine the components defined here. Plural forms such as AFVs, MMCs, and SSRs use the singular entry.

Guidance.Heading: Case and context distinctions
Guidance.Text:
| Forms | Distinction |
|---|---|
| `DR` / `dr`; `DRM` / `drm` | Multiple dice versus one die, and the corresponding modifier. |
| `DM` / `dm` | Desperation Morale versus a dismantled weapon. |
| `HT` / `ht` | Heavy Tank versus halftrack. |
| `SP` / `sP`; `SD` / `sD` | Self-propelled versus Smoke Pots; Sand Dune overlay versus Smoke Discharger. |
| `MC` | Morale Check in rules; motorcycle in the vehicle Type column; Mortar Carrier in U.S. halftrack names. |
| `SR`; `RF`; `CS` | Spotting Round or side/rear facing; Rarity Factor or Red Factories; Crew Survival or close-support equipment variant. |
| `PRC` | Passengers, Riders, and Inherent Crew in rules; People's Republic of China in Chapter W historical footnotes. |
| `NA`; `UK`; `SL` | Not Allowed or North Africa; Unconfirmed Kill or the dotted U.K. national designation; Searchlight or the earlier Squad Leader game. |
| `L`, `H`, `T`, `B`, `F` | Listing column and counter position determine the meaning. See the individual entries. |
| `HOB` / `HoB` | Heat of Battle, including the chart typography. |
| `AOV`; `AS`; `GP`; `CA` | Armoured Observation Vehicle; Aerosan movement or Italian Autosahariana; Ground Pressure or Belgian Grande Portée; Covered Arc, French support company, or Contre Avions. Context selects the meaning. |
| `C#` | Canister Depletion Number in ammo notation; Canister Firepower in the IFT legend. |
| `A#` | APCR Depletion Number in ammunition notation; British War Office designation in tank names. |
| `FL` / `FL#` | Fire Lane versus a Fortified Building Location in the Cave-Complex Setup Sheet legend. |

Guidance.Heading: Reading compound and qualified forms
Guidance.Text:
- Vehicle types are compositional. For example `AAtr` combines Anti-Aircraft and truck, `TDht` combines Tank Destroyer and halftrack, and `MTv` combines Medium Tank and variant. The Vehicle Listings Key on p. 338 supplies the components; a national vehicle note can add restrictions.
- A leading weapon-mount code, such as `T75L` or `B75L`, identifies turret or bow/non-turreted mounting followed by caliber and barrel length. It is not a new acronym for each caliber. See D1.8, C2.21, C4.1, and the Vehicle Listings Key on p. 338.
- An ammunition letter followed by a number, such as `A6`, `H7`, or `s8`, combines an ammunition type and a Depletion Number. A superscript can qualify its availability date. See C8.1-C8.9 and the Vehicle Listings Key on p. 338. Vehicular smoke-dispenser Usage Numbers are governed separately by D13.
- A number prefixed to `MC`, `KIA`, or `PAATC` qualifies the result or check; a suffix such as `#` means Number. See A7.301-A7.304, A10.1, A11.6, and the symbol key on p. 42. A #MC is governed by A7.304, and K/# has its own Casualty Reduction procedure in A7.302.
- `CG-LVP`, `FL RFP`, `CC Reaction Fire`, `Non-CC`, `MA AAMG`, and `SW/Gun` combine terms already defined here. Apply the cited rule for the combination rather than treating it as a new independent capability.
- Counter symbols such as concealment `?`, the radioless mark, the unarmored mark, and the leadership-exclusion triangle are graphic notation. Their explanations are in the symbol key on p. 42 and A.10, A12, D1.21, and D14. A text extractor can substitute letters for these symbols.

Guidance.Heading: Scan record
Guidance.Text:
This reference contains 438 alphabetical entries and 247 equipment, historical, or publication entries. All 685 entries received abbreviation and expanded-name/context searches across all 716 pages of the hash-verified original PDF. Searches included plural, punctuation, hyphenation, accented-letter, British/American spelling, suffix, and compound-code variants where applicable. Search hits were checked against the surrounding source passages before being used as definition citations.

The [expanded-term search ledger](ASL%20Acronym%20Expanded-Term%20Search%20Ledger.csv) records each entry, the search strings and short-form variants, physical pages with matches, per-query expanded-term page maps, the resulting definition/source references, and the remaining-review disposition and source basis. A page match is a search lead, not a claim that every occurrence defines the term. Broad context searches can include unrelated uses of the same words or letters.

Compared with the pre-audit document, 175 entries changed (127 alphabetical and 48 supplementary). The changes include numbered definitions for foxhole capacities, overlay prefixes, Armored Cars, Railroads, and Line of Fire; recovered BT, KV, KNIL, GSW, and HVAP expansions; the two meanings of Gun Type; Hand-to-Hand CC qualifications; and additional designer-note and equipment-note citations. Exact duplicate rule citations were consolidated. The former blanket statement about an absent numbered defining rule has been removed.

The remaining-510 review is complete (2026-10-26). Its scope was the 311 alphabetical and 199 supplementary entries left unchanged by the preceding 175-entry audit. All 510 received renewed abbreviation and expanded-name/context searches across the original 716-page PDF and a passage-level check of their definitions and contributing citations. This pass changed 276 entries and retained 234 after review. The ledger records a disposition and source basis for every entry in that scope, including entries needing no change. The 175 earlier entries remain separately identified.

Corrections include the explicit BA, TACAM, StuG, StuIG, and StuPz names; the HVSS and LVT(A) vehicle-note numbers; NKVD's defining footnote; Mortar Carrier as another MC meaning; General Purpose as another GP meaning; British War Office A# designations; and the different meanings of L in equipment names. The review also adds primary rule explanations for movement, fire, morale, ammunition, and vehicle codes, and distinguishes conventional expansions from names actually spelled out in the PDF.

Verification retained all 685 entries, checked the Markdown against the CSV by entry identity, and rechecked the original PDF hash. The AFV destruction table, Vehicle Listings Key, British Vehicle Listing, and Polish turret diagram were also inspected visually on physical pages 176, 338, 403, and 499. External historical/solitaire rules remain external locators, not verified rule text. Search hit lists document discovery; they are not a claim that every hit contributes to a definition.

Targeted verification on 2026-10-26 found that the earlier OC entry had missed an explicit numbered definition. A fresh extraction of the original PDF contains 36 case-insensitive occurrences of Ocean overlay or Ocean overlays when whitespace and hyphenated forms are included, on physical pages 15, 31, 46, 308, 309, 313, 317, 319, 324, 326, 678, and 708. Of those, 32 use whitespace rather than a hyphen. There are five standalone OC occurrences, on pages 31, 308, 326, and 708; page 31 contains two. These are text occurrences, including repeated chart printings, not counts of distinct rules. G13.1 and G13.12 on p. 308 establish the definition and its Ocean/Lake/River scope. The corrected OC entry follows the expanded term into its supporting rules and applications rather than relying on its glossary label.

This is a definition reference with contributing rule and note citations, not an index of every occurrence. External historical and Solitaire rule locators remain identified as external because their rule text is absent from this PDF. Graphic symbols, model numbers, national note letters, personal initials, and layout filenames are excluded from acronym counts.
